Subject: HealthMint DPA: clarification on SCCs and processor roles

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the call earlier. We reviewed the draft DPA and have a few clarifying questions before we loop in procurement. Attached is a short list of questions from Legal (HealthMint_DPA_Questions.pdf). Top items:

- Confirm which EU SCCs module Redwood intends to rely on and whether the DPA will include a Transfer Impact Addendum for our EU data subjects.
- We need clarity on the processor/subprocessor process: are we able to get a standing subprocessor roster and 30-day notice for new subprocessors?
- A customer-side liability carveout for security incidents tied to misconfiguration — our team flagged that clause 7.2 (liability) is redlined and needs alignment.

Can you confirm a target timeline for internal legal review and, if possible, a one-hour alignment call early next week?

Thanks,
Oliver

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-10 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HealthMint DPA: clarification on SCCs and processor roles

Mina / Karthik —

I reviewed the HealthMint redlines and drafted a commercial-focused response. Attaching Redline_MSAV2.docx and Redline_DPA_20261210.docx. High level summary for the thread:

1) Cross-border transfers / SCCs: propose we accept EU SCCs (standard modules) plus a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) documenting technical and organizational measures. This avoids bespoke vendor law rewrites while meeting HealthMint's compliance needs.

2) Subprocessors: we’ll commit to providing the current roster and a 30-day notice for new subprocessors. We should not agree to a customer right to veto new subprocessors; instead offer an escalation/mitigation path (audit + suspension rights tied to material breach).

3) Liability carveout: we will keep the standard liability cap language but accept a narrowly tailored exception for proven Redwood misconfiguration leading to data leakage; suggest specific threshold language rather than an open carveout.

4) Security controls: confirm encryption at rest, in transit, SOC 2 Type II reports available on request, and retention of audit logs for 12 months. Karthik, include the technical evidence checklist in the TIA.

If HealthMint insists on changes outside these parameters, we should escalate to Sales for commercial concessions.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Data Privacy, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redline_MSAV2.docx, Redline_DPA_20261210.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: HealthMint DPA: clarification on SCCs and processor roles

Team —

Quick legal guidance to keep things tidy for HealthMint’s review:

- SCCs: recommend we include the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (controller-to-processor modules) verbatim in an annex and reference them in the DPA. Draft the Transfer Impact Addendum as a short exhibit that cites specific controls (encryption keys, access control, logging).

- Roles: ensure the DPA contains a table listing responsibilities (controller vs processor) and a requirement for Redwood to notify HealthMint 30 days in advance of new subprocessors, with a right to ask reasonable mitigation steps. Do not give HealthMint a unilateral veto — instead offer an expedited review timeline and potential suspension path for critical concerns.

- Evidence: provide a link to our SOC 2 cover letter + an itemized evidence manifest for the TIA. Keep commercial concessions (liability) as a last-resort negotiation item and only after Procurement indicates commitment.

Please finalize the redline and a 1-page cover memo for Oliver that lays out Option A (standard SCCs + TIA) vs Option B (SCCs + limited extra warranties) with recommended tradeoffs. I can review the memo before it goes out.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
